text:
Diego: Quick heads-up — we hit a canary accounting problem this morning when smart-routing fell back due to regional GPU pressure. The rollout UI showed 5% exposure but the experiment effectively saw ~3% because fallback rewrote the variant header.
Marta: Ugh. Did the trace show assigned vs executed variant?
Diego: No, our routing only exported the executed_variant. The assigned decision is buried in placement logs.
Ava: That explains the false-negative in the quality dashboard. PMs thought 5% got v2. They didn't.
Jin: Current behavior: placement decides assigned_variant -> routing may swap to executed_variant on fallback, and we only tag executed_variant in traces. So telemetry and billing diverge.
Product-Liz: This is scary for launch metrics and A/B conclusions. We need to show "intended" vs "actual" exposure in Console and flag heavy fallback.
Marta: Proposal: enrich the trace schema and placement API to include assigned_variant and fallback_reason, then surface both in aggregations.
Diego: Agreed. Minimal change: routing returns assigned_variant + executed_variant + optional fallback_reason. That avoids reconstructing from logs.
Ava: Implementation question: do we change the internal placement API signature or just have routing emit an additional trace tag?
Jin: We should change placement return shape to include assigned_variant (string) and fallback_reason (nullable string). Routing already has the info during decision time.
ops-janet: Also consider billing/usage: executed_variant debit is correct for resource accounting, but experiment attribution should also record assigned bucket. So we need dual attribution in analytics.
sre-bot: Alert: fallback_rate(us-west, Standard) > 1.8% for 15m.
Marta: UX: Console rollout page should show three columns per bucket: intended_exposure, actual_exposure, fallback_rate. Add a tiny sparkline and hourly buckets for debugging.
Product-Liz: Also add a customer-facing toggle for strict scope enforcement. If enabled, routing should refuse to serve outside scoped variants and surface a "blocked" state instead of falling back. Some customers prefer strict scoping over availability.
Diego: Good point. New rollout field: strict_scope_enforcement (bool). Default false to preserve current availability-first behavior.
Ava: From alerting side, we should create a rollout-level circuit-breaker metric: fallback_incident_count and fallback_rate. If fallback_rate > threshold for >5m, auto-pause rollout or notify.
Jin: One tricky thing: we sample traces for Standard tier to limit cost. Pre-aggregator needs to estimate actual counts with a sampling correction factor or use assignment stream (which is cheap) combined with executed traces to compute fallback_rate.
Marta: So design: stream assignments into an hourly pre-aggregator keyed by (customer_id, tier, region, rollout_id, assigned_variant) and join with executed_variant traces (sampled) to estimate executed counts and fallback incidence.
Diego: That work splits nicely: routing + trace schema change first, then pre-aggregator for Console metrics, then UI. Prioritize telemetry so PMs stop making bad decisions.
ops-janet: I'll reserve infra cycles for a small pre-aggregator job and runbook. Need expected cardinality estimates. Jin, can you mock numbers?
Jin: Yes — I'll post a short spreadsheet with estimated keys per hour and sample rates, and recommend retention and bucket sizes. Retain assigned_variant for 30 days.
Ava: I'll open a tiny PR to add assigned_variant to the trace exporter schema and add docs for the new rollout flag.
Marta: Also add a note to rollout docs that fallback counts as executed for resource billing, assigned for experiment attribution. Keep that language explicit.
Diego: Action items summary:
- Jin: placement API patch + cardinality spreadsheet + migration notes
- Ava: trace schema PR + docs update + alerting playbook change
- ops-janet: infra slot + pre-aggregator runbook
- Marta/Product-Liz: Console mock for intended vs actual exposure, strict_scope toggle UX
deploy-bot: Deployed trace-schema preview to staging (build 2026.4.01.12).
Ava: I'll run e2e in staging once Jin's mock data lands.
Diego: Thanks all. Goal: get telemetry fix out this week before increasing canary exposures. Keep thread updated with links to PRs and mockups.
